AsyncTaskStatus.description:
AsyncTask status:
* `pending` - Task is queued and waiting to be processed
* `processing` - Task is currently being processed
* `completed` - Task completed successfully
* `failed` - Task failed with an error

AsyncTaskType.description:
AsyncTask type:
**Segment operations:**
* `segment.add_to_group` - Add segment members to a group
* `segment.remove_from_group` - Remove segment members from a group
* `segment.export` - Export segment members to file
* `segment.unsubscribe` - Unsubscribe segment members
* `segment.delete_contacts` - Delete segment members

**Group operations:**
* `group.export` - Export group members to file
* `group.clear` - Remove all members from group
* `group.add_from_segment` - Add members from segment to group
* `group.remove_from_segment` - Remove members from segment from group
* `group.add_from_conditions` - Add members matching conditions to group
* `group.remove_from_conditions` - Remove members matching conditions from group

AttributeStatus.description:
Attribute status:
* `active` - Accepts new values
* `archived` - Keeps its stored values but no longer accepts new ones

AutomationStep.AutomationStepAddToGroup-.description:
API Resource for automation steps.

This class defines the API endpoints and serves as the base class for all
automation step types. Uses DiscriminatorMap for polymorphic serialization.

parent.description: IRI of the step after which this one is placed (/automations/{uuid}/automation_steps/{uuid}). It cannot be a condition step: use `parent_yes` or `parent_no` for those. Send at most one of `parent`, `parent_yes` and `parent_no`; send none to make this the first step, which is only possible while the automation has no first step.

parent_no.description: IRI of a condition step; this step is placed in its 'no' branch (contacts that do not meet the condition). Only valid for condition steps. Send at most one position field.

parent_yes.description: IRI of a condition step; this step is placed in its 'yes' branch (contacts that meet the condition). Only valid for condition steps. Send at most one position field.

AutomationStep.jsonld-automation.read_au.description:
API Resource for automation steps.

This class defines the API endpoints and serves as the base class for all
automation step types. Uses DiscriminatorMap for polymorphic serialization.

action.description:
Action configuration. Structure depends on step_type:

- **step.delay**: DelayAction (delay_value, delay_unit, time settings)
- **step.condition**: ConditionAction (match, conditions array)
- **step.send.campaign**: SendCampaignAction (subject, from_name, template_html, etc.)
- **step.send.sms**: SendSmsAction (title, message, sms_sender, tracking fields)
- **step.add.to.group**: AddToGroupAction (group IRI)
- **step.remove.from.group**: RemoveFromGroupAction (group IRI)
- **step.update.custom.field**: UpdateCustomFieldAction (field IRI, value)
- **step.update.score**: UpdateScoreAction (value -5..5)
- **step.send.notification**: SendNotificationAction (emails, subject, body)
- **step.trigger.automation**: TriggerAutomationAction (automation IRI)
- **step.unsuscribe**: UnsubscribeAction (empty object)
- **step.move.to.step**: MoveToStepAction (target step IRI)
- **step.send.webhook**: SendWebhookAction (url, secret, payload_items)

children.description:
Child steps. Structure depends on step_type:

- **Normal steps** (delay, send_campaign, etc.): `{ "next": AutomationStep | null }`
- **Condition steps**: `{ "yes": AutomationStep | null, "no": AutomationStep | null }`

uuid.description: Resource UUID

CampaignDeferredBatchCount.description:
Campaign deferredBatchCount:
Defines the number of batches the campaign will be split into.
Used with `incremental` and `fixed_batches_by_count` strategies.
The system will calculate the size of each batch automatically based on the total number of recipients.
Example: 5 → campaign will be sent in 5 equal or progressively sized batches.

CampaignDeferredBatchSize.description:
Campaign deferredBatchSize:
Defines the number of recipients to send in each batch (used with fixed_batches_by_size strategy).

CampaignDeferredInterval.description:
Campaign deferredInterval:
Defines the interval between each batch (e.g., 30 minutes, 1 hour).

CampaignDeferredStrategy.description:
Campaign deferredStrategy:
* `incremental` - Sends the campaign in a predefined number of batches at regular intervals. Each batch increases in size automatically.
* `fixed_batches_by_size` - Sends a fixed number of recipients in each batch (e.g., 5,000 recipients every 30 minutes).
* `fixed_batches_by_count` - Sends the campaign in a predefined number of batches, automatically calculating the size of each batch (e.g., 5 batches every 30 minutes).

CampaignDeliveryWarningCode.description:
Campaign delivery warning codes:
* `campaign.delivery_warning.no_active_subscribers` - No active subscribers (danger, blocks sending)
* `campaign.delivery_warning.insufficient_credits` - Insufficient credits (danger, blocks sending)
* `campaign.delivery_warning.daily_limit_exceeded` - Daily limit exceeded (warning, blocks sending)
* `campaign.delivery_warning.send_disabled` - Sending disabled (danger, blocks sending)
* `campaign.delivery_warning.approval_required` - Approval required (danger, blocks sending)
* `campaign.delivery_warning.approval_pending` - Approval pending (danger, blocks sending)
* `campaign.delivery_warning.cannot_send_without_authenticate` - Cannot send >1000 without auth (danger, blocks sending)
* `campaign.delivery_warning.sender_domain_not_authenticated` - Domain not authenticated (warning)
* `campaign.delivery_warning.custom_tracking_links_error` - Tracking links SSL/DNS error (warning)
* `campaign.delivery_warning.free_email_provider` - Free email provider (warning)
* `campaign.delivery_warning.domain_authentication_not_created` - Domain auth not created (warning)

CampaignSendTo.description:
Campaign sendTo:
* `send_to_all` - Send to all
* `send_to_segment` - Send to a saved segment
* `send_to_groups` - Send to one or more groups

Company.description:
Companies of the public API (plan fase 3, Tasks 19 and 20). Generated from the approved proposal by
fase-3/tools/gen_company_read.py (reads) and gen_company_writes.py (create, update, delete) and edited by hand
afterwards: the texts are the proposal's. The writes check the CRM access in their processor (and the delete in
its provider) before anything else, because API Platform evaluates `security` after the provider.

`company:list` is the summary every item of the list has; `company:detail` adds what only `get_company` returns.
`attributes` is an \ArrayObject so that an empty one is published as `{}`, not as `[]` (`preserve_empty_objects`).

annual_revenue.description: Annual revenue range, in the given currency. This is the company's own revenue range, not the account's ARR. A range needs `min` and `currency`. `null` clears it.

Contact.ContactCreateInput.description:
Contacts of the public API (plan fase 3, Task 16): the person, one record whatever the audiences they belong to.
Generated from the approved proposal by fase-3/tools/gen_contact_read.py and edited by hand afterwards: the texts
are the proposal's. Reads over ReadContacts; the writes (Tasks 17-18) are added to this resource.

additional_emails.description: Other email addresses of the same person. They identify the contact (for example to match incoming emails) but are never subscribed to an audience: only the primary `email` is used by marketing. Replaces the whole list; send `[]` to remove them.

additional_phones.description: Other phone numbers of the same person, in E.164 format. Never used by marketing, only the primary `phone` is. Replaces the whole list; send `[]` to remove them.

attributes.description: Attribute values keyed by the attribute `public_code`, for example `{"lead_source": "Webinar"}`. Get the codes, types and options with `list_contact_attributes`. `enum` and `multi_enum` attributes accept the UUID of an option or its exact label; `money` is `{amount, currency}`; `null` removes the value. An unknown or archived code is rejected with a 422. Attributes you leave out keep their value.

company.description: IRI of the company the contact works for (`/companies/{uuid}`). A contact has at most one company; changing or removing it does not affect their audiences, tasks or opportunities. Setting it requires a CRM seat and the `crm.contacts_companies.write` capability. The company must already exist: create it first with `create_company`. `null` removes the link.

description.example: Met at the Madrid e-commerce summit.

email.description: Primary email address. At least one of `email` or `phone` is required. It must not belong to another contact of the account (the other contact is not merged or updated).

facebook_url.description: Facebook profile, as a username (with or without `@`) or a URL. It is stored and returned as the full URL.

instagram_url.description: Instagram profile, as a username (with or without `@`) or a URL. It is stored and returned as the full URL.

job_title.description: Job title as free text (up to 190 characters).

linkedin_url.description: LinkedIn profile, as a username (with or without `@`) or a URL. It is stored and returned as the full URL.

locale.description: Language and region of the person, as a locale code such as `es_ES` or `en_US`.

location.description: Where the person lives. All fields are optional. Fields you leave out keep their value.

owner.description: Email of the user of the account in charge of this contact, exactly as they sign in. It must be an active user of the account. `null` leaves the contact without owner. Being the owner does not change who can see the contact.

phone.description: Primary phone number in E.164 format. At least one of `email` or `phone` is required. It must not belong to another contact.

tags.description: Tags of the contact, each one as the UUID of an existing tag or its name. A name that matches no tag (ignoring case) creates that tag. Check the existing tags with `list_contact_tags` first, so you reuse them instead of creating near-duplicates.

x_url.description: X profile, as a username (with or without `@`) or a URL. It is stored and returned as the full URL.

are the proposal's. Reads over ReadContacts; the writes (Tasks 17-18) are added to this resource.

additional_emails.description: Other email addresses of the same person. They identify the contact (for example to match incoming emails) but are never subscribed to an audience: only the primary `email` is used by marketing. Replaces the whole list; send `[]` to remove them. Left unchanged if omitted.

additional_phones.description: Other phone numbers of the same person, in E.164 format. Never used by marketing, only the primary `phone` is. Replaces the whole list; send `[]` to remove them. Left unchanged if omitted.

attributes.description: Attribute values keyed by the attribute `public_code`, for example `{"lead_source": "Webinar"}`. Get the codes, types and options with `list_contact_attributes`. `enum` and `multi_enum` attributes accept the UUID of an option or its exact label; `money` is `{amount, currency}`; `null` removes the value. An unknown or archived code is rejected with a 422. Attributes you leave out keep their value.

birth_date.description: Birth date as `YYYY-MM-DD`. Left unchanged if omitted.

company.description: IRI of the company the contact works for (`/companies/{uuid}`). A contact has at most one company; changing or removing it does not affect their audiences, tasks or opportunities. Setting it requires a CRM seat and the `crm.contacts_companies.write` capability. The company must already exist: create it first with `create_company`. `null` removes the link. Left unchanged if omitted.

description.description: Free-text notes about the person. Left unchanged if omitted.
description.example: Met at the Madrid e-commerce summit.

email.description: Primary email address. `null` removes it, only if the contact keeps a phone. It must not belong to another contact of the account (the other contact is not merged or updated). A different email keeps the person subscribed where they were confirmed (see the operation description).

facebook_url.description: Facebook profile, as a username (with or without `@`) or a URL. It is stored and returned as the full URL. Left unchanged if omitted.

first_name.description: First name (up to 255 characters). Left unchanged if omitted.

instagram_url.description: Instagram profile, as a username (with or without `@`) or a URL. It is stored and returned as the full URL. Left unchanged if omitted.

job_title.description: Job title as free text (up to 190 characters). Left unchanged if omitted.

last_name.description: Last name (up to 255 characters). Left unchanged if omitted.

linkedin_url.description: LinkedIn profile, as a username (with or without `@`) or a URL. It is stored and returned as the full URL. Left unchanged if omitted.

locale.description: Language and region of the person, as a locale code such as `es_ES` or `en_US`. Left unchanged if omitted.

location.description: Where the person lives. All fields are optional. Fields you leave out keep their value.

owner.description: Email of the user of the account in charge of this contact, exactly as they sign in. It must be an active user of the account. `null` leaves the contact without owner. Being the owner does not change who can see the contact.

phone.description: Primary phone number in E.164 format. `null` removes it, only if the contact keeps an email. It must not belong to another contact. A different number keeps the person subscribed to SMS where they were confirmed (see the operation description).

tags.description: Tags of the contact, each one as the UUID of an existing tag or its name. A name that matches no tag (ignoring case) creates that tag. Check the existing tags with `list_contact_tags` first, so you reuse them instead of creating near-duplicates. Replaces the whole set; send `[]` to remove all the tags. Left unchanged if omitted.

x_url.description: X profile, as a username (with or without `@`) or a URL. It is stored and returned as the full URL. Left unchanged if omitted.

ContactAttributeType.description:
Contact attributes attribute type:
* `text` - Short text
* `long_text` - Long text, several lines
* `integer` - Whole number
* `decimal` - Decimal number
* `percentage` - Percentage
* `money` - Amount of money in the currency of the attribute
* `boolean` - Yes or no
* `date` - Calendar date
* `datetime` - Date and time
* `birthday` - Birthday (day and month, year optional)
* `enum` - One option from a list
* `multi_enum` - Several options from a list
* `email` - Email address
* `phone` - Phone number
* `url` - Web address
* `country` - Country (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code)
* `language` - Language (ISO 639-1 code)
* `timezone` - IANA time zone name

* `user` - A person of the account
* `contact` - A contact
* `automation` - An automation
* `integration` - An integration
* `system` - Easymailing itself
* `external` - Someone outside the account

CrmInitiatedVia.description:

* `ui` - From the Easymailing app
* `maia` - By Maia, the assistant, on behalf of a person
* `api` - Through the API
* `import` - By a file import
* `sync` - By a synchronization with a connected service
* `automation` - By an automation
* `system` - By Easymailing itself

CrmRecordSource.description:

date_year.description: Calendar date and time when the wait ends, in the contact's time zone. It must be later than the start of today; if the moment has already passed, the contact continues at once. Required for the calendar-date wait.

day_month.description: Day of the month on which the wait ends; 0 means the last day of the month. Required for the day-of-month wait.

day_week.description: Weekdays on which the contact may continue (0 = Sunday, 1 = Monday, ... 6 = Saturday). Required for the weekday wait. Known issue: the engine that resumes the contact reads weekday names, so this wait may leave the contact stuck; prefer another unit.

delay_unit.description: Kind of wait: a relative amount of time (minutes, hours, days or weeks) or a fixed moment (a time of day, weekdays, a day of the month or a calendar date).

delay_value.description: Amount of time to wait, in units of `delay_unit`. Required for the relative waits (minutes, hours, days or weeks).

Note.description:
Notes of the public API (plan fase 4, Task 19). Generated from the approved proposal by fase-4/tools/gen_notes.py and
edited by hand afterwards: the texts are the proposal's. Every operation checks the CRM access in its provider or
processor before anything else, because API Platform evaluates `security` after the provider.

`list_notes` pages by cursor (`paginationViaCursor` goes on the resource: on the operation API Platform 3.4.17 loses
it) and gives the total of the record. `cursor` is the opaque position of each item, which API Platform copies into
the `cursor[gt]` of `hydra:next` (the last item) and the `cursor[lt]` of `hydra:previous` (the first one); it is never
published.

body_html.description: Text of the note as limited HTML (paragraphs, headings, lists, bold, italic, underline, links and images).
body_html.example: Ana wants the annual plan with quarterly billing.

can_delete.description: Whether the user who owns the token can delete this note: the same people who can edit it.

can_edit.description: Whether the user who owns the token can edit this note: its author or an account admin with a token that reaches account administration (an API key, or OAuth with the `admin` scope).

created_at.description: When the note was created, ISO 8601.

created_by.description: Author of the note. `null` when unknown.

kind.description: Kind of actor: `user` for a person, otherwise `contact`, `automation`, `integration`, `system` or `external`.

name.description: Name of the actor. `null` when the person is no longer a member of the account.

preview_text.description: Plain-text start of the note, up to 280 characters, to show it in a list.
preview_text.example: Ana wants the annual plan with quarterly billing.

record.description: IRI of the contact, company or opportunity the note belongs to. A note belongs to exactly one record and never moves.

record_type.description: Kind of record the note belongs to.

title.description: Optional title of the note. `null` when it has none.

updated_at.description: When the note last changed, ISO 8601.

updated_by.description: Who last edited the note; the author when it was never edited. `null` when unknown.

kind.description: Kind of actor: `user` for a person, otherwise `contact`, `automation`, `integration`, `system` or `external`.

name.description: Name of the actor. `null` when the person is no longer a member of the account.

uuid.description: UUID of the note.

version.description: Version of the note; it grows with every edit. Send it as `expected_version` to make sure nobody edited the note in between.

processor before anything else, because API Platform evaluates `security` after the provider.

`list_notes` pages by cursor (`paginationViaCursor` goes on the resource: on the operation API Platform 3.4.17 loses
it) and gives the total of the record. `cursor` is the opaque position of each item, which API Platform copies into
the `cursor[gt]` of `hydra:next` (the last item) and the `cursor[lt]` of `hydra:previous` (the first one); it is never
published.

body_html.description: New text of the note, replacing the whole previous text. Limited HTML: paragraphs, line breaks, headings, lists, bold, italic, underline, links (`http`, `https`, `mailto`) and images; anything else is removed. At most 10,000 visible characters and 60,000 bytes. It cannot be empty.
body_html.example: Ana wants the annual plan with monthly billing.

expected_version.description: Version of the note you read (`version`). Optional: if you send it and the note has changed since, nothing is saved and you get `crm_note_version_conflict`; if you leave it out, the change is applied over the current text.

title.description: Title of the note, up to 200 characters. `null` removes it.

Opportunity.description:
Opportunities of the public API (plan fase 4, Tasks 13 and 14). Generated from the approved proposal by
fase-4/tools/gen_opportunity_read.py and edited by hand afterwards: the texts are the proposal's. The providers
check the CRM capability and the pipeline level before anything else, because API Platform evaluates `security`
after the provider.

`opportunity:list` is the summary every item of the list has; `opportunity:detail` adds what only `get_opportunity`
returns. `attributes` is an \ArrayObject so that an empty one is published as `{}`, not as `[]`.

attributes.description: Attribute values keyed by `public_code` (see `list_opportunity_attributes`). `enum` and `multi_enum` values are `{uuid, label}`, `money` is `{amount, currency}`. Attributes without value are omitted.

closed_at.description: When it was won or lost. `null` while it is open; reopening clears it.

company.description: IRI of the company (`/companies/{uuid}`). `null` when there is none.

contacts.description: IRIs of the contacts (`/contacts/{uuid}`) linked to the opportunity. There is no primary contact.

created_by.description: Person who created it. `null` when that user no longer exists.

uuid.description: UUID of the user.

description.example: Renewal of the annual plan with a seat upgrade.

expected_close_date.description: Date the deal is expected to close (`YYYY-MM-DD`).

loss_note.description: Free-text note given when it was lost.
loss_note.example: Chose a competitor with a lower price.

loss_reason.description: Reason it was lost. `null` when it is not lost or none was given.

uuid.description: UUID of the loss reason.

owner.description: User in charge of the opportunity. `null` when there is none. An owner who was deactivated stays assigned.

email.description: Email of the user; send it in `owner` to assign this user.

uuid.description: UUID of the user.

pipeline.description: IRI of the pipeline the opportunity belongs to (`/pipelines/{uuid}`).

probability.description: Effective win probability, 0 to 100. It is the stage probability unless `probability_mode` is `custom`; 100 when won and 0 when lost.

probability_mode.description: `stage` when the probability comes from the stage, `custom` when someone overrode it (only open stages of pipelines that allow it).

record_source.description: How the opportunity was created: `manual`, `api`, `automation`, `import`... It never changes.

reference_value.description: Value in the reference currency of the pipeline, calculated by the server. `null` when the opportunity has no amount.

amount.description: Amount converted to the reference currency. `null` while the conversion is pending or unavailable.

basis.description: `latest` for the latest rate, `closure` for the rate of the closing date of a won or lost opportunity.

currency.description: Reference currency of the pipeline.

rate_date.description: Date of the exchange rate used. `null` when no conversion was needed.

status.description: `same_currency`, `converted`, `pending` (no rate yet) or `unavailable`.

weighted_amount.description: Converted amount multiplied by the effective probability (the forecast).

stage.description: Current stage of the opportunity. `null` when it has no stage (it is open and shows in the «no stage» column).

type.description: Stage type: `open`, `won` or `lost`.

uuid.description: UUID of the stage.

stage_entered_at.description: When the opportunity entered its current stage.

status.description: Commercial situation, derived from the stage type: `open`, `won` or `lost`. An opportunity without stage is `open`.

uuid.description: UUID of the opportunity.

value.description: Amount and currency of the opportunity. `null` when it has no amount.

amount.description: Decimal amount as a string, never a float.

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency code. It must be one the pipeline accepts.

Opportunity.OpportunityCreateInput.description:
Opportunities of the public API (plan fase 4, Tasks 13 and 14). Generated from the approved proposal by
fase-4/tools/gen_opportunity_read.py and edited by hand afterwards: the texts are the proposal's. The providers
check the CRM capability and the pipeline level before anything else, because API Platform evaluates `security`
after the provider.

`opportunity:list` is the summary every item of the list has; `opportunity:detail` adds what only `get_opportunity`
returns. `attributes` is an \ArrayObject so that an empty one is published as `{}`, not as `[]`.

attributes.description: Values of the account's opportunity attributes, keyed by `public_code` (see `list_opportunity_attributes`). `enum` and `multi_enum` accept the option UUID or its exact label; `money` is `{amount, currency}`; `null` removes a value. Attributes you leave out keep their value.

company.description: IRI of an existing company (`/companies/{uuid}`). `null` removes the link. Linking a company does not change the contacts and the other way round.

contacts.description: IRIs of the contacts of the opportunity (`/contacts/{uuid}`), up to 500. Replaces the whole set; send `[]` to remove all of them.

description.example: Renewal of the annual plan with a seat upgrade.

loss_note.description: Free-text note about the loss, up to 10000 characters.

loss_reason.description: Reason for losing it: the UUID of a loss reason of the pipeline or its exact name (`get_pipeline`, `loss_reasons`). Archived reasons cannot be used. Whether it is required, optional or not allowed depends on `loss_reason_mode` of the lost stage.

owner.description: Email of the user in charge, exactly as they sign in. It must be an active user with access to the pipeline. `null` leaves the opportunity without owner. Nobody is assigned if you leave it out: there is no default owner for the API.

pipeline.description: IRI of the pipeline (`/pipelines/{uuid}`) where the deal starts. Get it from `list_pipelines`. The user needs `work` access to it.

probability.description: Overrides the stage probability, 0 to 99. Allowed only while the opportunity is in an open stage of a pipeline with `allow_custom_probability`. `null` goes back to the probability of the stage.

stage.description: Stage of that pipeline: its UUID or its exact name (`get_pipeline`). Leave it out to create the opportunity without stage; it then sits in the «no stage» column with probability 0. If you pick the stage, its entry requirements must be met by the values you send. Picking a won or lost stage creates the deal already closed.

title.description: Name of the opportunity. Required to create it; it cannot be `null`.

value.description: Amount and currency. The currency must be in the platform exchange-rate catalog and, if the pipeline does not allow several currencies, equal to its reference currency. `null` clears both.

amount.description: Decimal amount as a string, never a float.

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency code. It must be one the pipeline accepts.

Opportunity.OpportunityUpdateInput.description:
Opportunities of the public API (plan fase 4, Tasks 13 and 14). Generated from the approved proposal by

after the provider.

`opportunity:list` is the summary every item of the list has; `opportunity:detail` adds what only `get_opportunity`
returns. `attributes` is an \ArrayObject so that an empty one is published as `{}`, not as `[]`.

attributes.description: Values of the account's opportunity attributes, keyed by `public_code` (see `list_opportunity_attributes`). `enum` and `multi_enum` accept the option UUID or its exact label; `money` is `{amount, currency}`; `null` removes a value. Attributes you leave out keep their value.

company.description: IRI of an existing company (`/companies/{uuid}`). `null` removes the link. Linking a company does not change the contacts and the other way round.

contacts.description: IRIs of the contacts of the opportunity (`/contacts/{uuid}`), up to 500. Replaces the whole set; send `[]` to remove all of them. Left unchanged if omitted.

description.example: Renewal of the annual plan with a seat upgrade.

owner.description: Email of the user in charge, exactly as they sign in. It must be an active user with access to the pipeline. `null` leaves the opportunity without owner. Nobody is assigned if you leave it out: there is no default owner for the API.

probability.description: Overrides the stage probability, 0 to 99. Allowed only while the opportunity is in an open stage of a pipeline with `allow_custom_probability`. `null` goes back to the probability of the stage.

title.description: Name of the opportunity. Required to create it; it cannot be `null`.

value.description: Amount and currency. The currency must be in the platform exchange-rate catalog and, if the pipeline does not allow several currencies, equal to its reference currency. `null` clears both.

amount.description: Decimal amount as a string, never a float.

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency code. It must be one the pipeline accepts.

Opportunity.jsonld.description:

attributes.description: Attribute values keyed by `public_code` (see `list_opportunity_attributes`). `enum` and `multi_enum` values are `{uuid, label}`, `money` is `{amount, currency}`. Attributes without value are omitted.

closed_at.description: When it was won or lost. `null` while it is open; reopening clears it.

company.description: IRI of the company (`/companies/{uuid}`). `null` when there is none.

contacts.description: IRIs of the contacts (`/contacts/{uuid}`) linked to the opportunity. There is no primary contact.

created_by.description: Person who created it. `null` when that user no longer exists.

uuid.description: UUID of the user.

description.example: Renewal of the annual plan with a seat upgrade.

expected_close_date.description: Date the deal is expected to close (`YYYY-MM-DD`).

iri.description: Hydra IRI for this entity (e.g. "/audiences/01HXXXX..."). Populated by the SDK from the response `@id`; consumers can use it to deep-link or correlate cross-resource relationships.

loss_note.description: Free-text note given when it was lost.
loss_note.example: Chose a competitor with a lower price.

loss_reason.description: Reason it was lost. `null` when it is not lost or none was given.

uuid.description: UUID of the loss reason.

owner.description: User in charge of the opportunity. `null` when there is none. An owner who was deactivated stays assigned.

email.description: Email of the user; send it in `owner` to assign this user.

uuid.description: UUID of the user.

pipeline.description: IRI of the pipeline the opportunity belongs to (`/pipelines/{uuid}`).

probability.description: Effective win probability, 0 to 100. It is the stage probability unless `probability_mode` is `custom`; 100 when won and 0 when lost.

probability_mode.description: `stage` when the probability comes from the stage, `custom` when someone overrode it (only open stages of pipelines that allow it).

record_source.description: How the opportunity was created: `manual`, `api`, `automation`, `import`... It never changes.

reference_value.description: Value in the reference currency of the pipeline, calculated by the server. `null` when the opportunity has no amount.

amount.description: Amount converted to the reference currency. `null` while the conversion is pending or unavailable.

basis.description: `latest` for the latest rate, `closure` for the rate of the closing date of a won or lost opportunity.

currency.description: Reference currency of the pipeline.

rate_date.description: Date of the exchange rate used. `null` when no conversion was needed.

status.description: `same_currency`, `converted`, `pending` (no rate yet) or `unavailable`.

weighted_amount.description: Converted amount multiplied by the effective probability (the forecast).

stage.description: Current stage of the opportunity. `null` when it has no stage (it is open and shows in the «no stage» column).

type.description: Stage type: `open`, `won` or `lost`.

uuid.description: UUID of the stage.

stage_entered_at.description: When the opportunity entered its current stage.

status.description: Commercial situation, derived from the stage type: `open`, `won` or `lost`. An opportunity without stage is `open`.

uuid.description: UUID of the opportunity.

value.description: Amount and currency of the opportunity. `null` when it has no amount.

amount.description: Decimal amount as a string, never a float.

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency code. It must be one the pipeline accepts.

OpportunityAttribute-opportunity_attribu.description:
Opportunity attributes of the public API (plan fase 4, Task 20): the definitions of the custom fields of a opportunity, over
AttributeDefinitionManager. Generated from the approved proposal by fase-4/tools/gen_opportunity_attributes.py and
edited by hand afterwards: the texts are the proposal's.

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency code. Only for `money` attributes; null for every other type.

current_value_count.description: Number of opportunities that currently have a value for this attribute.

description.description: Optional explanation of what the attribute holds.
description.example: Kind of deal the opportunity represents.

ever_used.description: True if the attribute or any of its options has ever held a value, even if it has none now.

iri.description: Hydra IRI for this entity (e.g. "/audiences/01HXXXX..."). Populated by the SDK from the response `@id`; consumers can use it to deep-link or correlate cross-resource relationships.

name.description: Visible name of the attribute, unique among the active opportunity attributes.

options.description: Options of an `enum` or `multi_enum` attribute, in display order. Empty for every other type.

integration_key.description: Stable key of the option for integrations. Never changes.

label.description: Visible name of the option.

position.description: Position of the option in the list, starting at 1.

status.description: `active` options can be assigned; `archived` options keep the values already stored but cannot be assigned again.

uuid.description: UUID of the option. Use it as the value of the attribute in a record.

OpportunityAttributeType.description:
Opportunity attribute type:
* `text` - Short text
* `long_text` - Long text, several lines
* `integer` - Whole number
* `decimal` - Decimal number
* `percentage` - Percentage
* `money` - Amount of money in the currency of the attribute
* `boolean` - Yes or no
* `date` - Calendar date
* `datetime` - Date and time
* `enum` - One option from a list
* `multi_enum` - Several options from a list
* `email` - Email address
* `phone` - Phone number
* `url` - Web address
* `country` - Country (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code)
* `language` - Language (ISO 639-1 code)
* `timezone` - IANA time zone name

OpportunityConversionStatus.description:
State of the conversion of an amount to a reference currency:
* `same_currency` - The amount is already in the reference currency
* `converted` - Converted with the rate of `rate_date`
* `pending` - There is no rate yet; the conversion is calculated later
* `unavailable` - The currency has no rate
* `no_amount` - The opportunity has no amount, so there is nothing to convert

OpportunityProbabilityMode.description:
Where the probability of an opportunity comes from:
* `stage` - The probability of the stage
* `custom` - A probability set by hand, allowed only in open stages of pipelines that permit it

OpportunityReferenceBasis.description:
Rate behind the reference value of an opportunity:
* `latest` - The latest rate
* `closure` - The rate of the closing date of a won or lost opportunity

OpportunityStatus.description:
Commercial situation of an opportunity, derived from the type of its stage:
* `open` - Being worked; also an opportunity without stage
* `won` - Closed as won
* `lost` - Closed as lost

Pipeline.description:
Pipelines of the public API (plan fase 4, Tasks 15 and 16). Generated from the approved proposal by
fase-4/tools/gen_pipeline_read.py and edited by hand afterwards: the texts are the proposal's.

`pipeline:list` is the summary every item of the list has; `pipeline:detail` adds what only `get_pipeline` returns
(the initial stage, the stages and the loss reasons).

access_level.description: Access of the user making the request to this pipeline: `read`, `work` or `admin`.

allow_custom_probability.description: Whether a deal in an open stage may override the probability of the stage.

allow_multiple_currencies.description: Whether deals may use currencies other than the reference currency.

default.description: true for the default pipeline of the account (exactly one).

initial_stage.description: UUID of the initial stage (an open stage). Deals created without stage do not use it.

loss_reasons.description: Loss reasons of the pipeline, active and archived, in order.

position.description: Position among the loss reasons: 0 is the first.

status.description: `active`, or `archived`: it can no longer be chosen but past deals keep it.

used.description: true when at least one closed deal uses it.

uuid.description: UUID of the loss reason.

name.description: Pipeline name, unique in the account (compared ignoring case).

reference_currency.description: Currency in which the forecast and totals of the pipeline are reported.

stages.description: Stages in order. Every pipeline has at least one open, one won and one lost stage.

loss_reason_mode.description: Only for lost stages: whether the loss reason is `required`, `optional` or `disabled` when a deal enters.

max_calendar_days.description: Calendar days a deal is expected to stay in this stage. `null` if there is no limit.

name.description: Stage name. Names are not forced to be unique; avoid repeating one, because operations that take a stage by name then ask for its UUID.

position.description: Position of the stage in the pipeline: 0 is the first.

probability.description: Win probability of deals in this stage: 0 to 99 for open stages, always 100 for won and 0 for lost.

required_attributes.description: `public_code` of the opportunity attributes a deal must have to enter this stage.

required_fields.description: Built-in fields a deal must have to enter this stage (`company`, `contacts`, `owner`, `amount_currency`, `expected_close_date`, `description`).

type.description: Stage type: `open` (the deal is being worked), `won` or `lost` (the deal is closed).

uuid.description: UUID of the stage.
UUID of the pipeline.

PipelineAccessLevel.description:
Access level of a user to a pipeline, from lowest to highest:
* `read` - See the pipeline and its opportunities
* `work` - Create and work opportunities
* `admin` - Manage the pipeline and delete its opportunities

PipelineLossReasonMode.description:
Whether a loss reason is asked when a deal enters a lost stage:
* `disabled` - No loss reason
* `optional` - A loss reason can be given
* `required` - A loss reason must be given

PipelineLossReasonStatus.description:
Loss reason status:
* `active` - Can be chosen
* `archived` - Can no longer be chosen; past deals keep it

PipelineStageType.description:
Pipeline stage type:
* `open` - The deal is being worked
* `won` - The deal is closed as won
* `lost` - The deal is closed as lost

display.description: Visual presentation, purely cosmetic (answers and stats are those of the base type). `rating` and `yes_no` always render as faces/thumbs: `smileys` uses emojis (the default) and `icons` uses app icons. `default` is accepted as a legacy value and resolves to `smileys`. Emails always fall back to emojis (email clients strip SVG) — for that reason `icons` is NOT accepted on poll questions (they are voted inside the email; 400 otherwise).

options.description: Answer options in display order (only for single_choice / multiple_choice / yes_no questions; scale types like rating/nps build their own scale). A yes_no question takes exactly two: first = 👍, second = 👎.

required.description: Whether the respondent must answer this question (defaults to true)

text.example: How satisfied are you with our newsletter?

type.description: Question type. `single_choice` and `multiple_choice` require `options` (2-10); `yes_no` requires EXACTLY two options — the first renders as 👍 and the second as 👎, with customizable texts; `rating` (1-5 scale), `nps` (Net Promoter Score, 0-10 scale) and `text` (open answer) must not have options.

Task.description:
Tasks of the public API (plan fase 4, Tasks 17 and 18). The reads are generated from the approved proposal by
fase-4/tools/gen_task_read.py and the writes by fase-4/tools/gen_task_write.py, edited by hand afterwards: the texts
are the proposal's. Every operation checks the
CRM access in its provider or processor before anything else, because API Platform evaluates `security` after the
provider.

`list_tasks` pages by cursor (`paginationViaCursor` goes on the resource: on the operation API Platform 3.4.17 loses
it) and gives no total. `cursor` is the opaque position of each task, which API Platform copies into the `cursor[gt]`
of `hydra:next` (the last item) and the `cursor[lt]` of `hydra:previous` (the first one); it is never published.
`assignee`, `completed_by` and `created_by` are arrays so that they keep the shape of the proposal; the related
records are {@see \App\Application\Crm\RecordRelationView} arrays.

assignee.description: User responsible for the task. `null` when it is unassigned.

email.description: Email of the user; send it in `assignee` to assign this user.

name.description: Full name of the user (their email when they have no name).

uuid.description: UUID of the user.

can_delete.description: Whether the user who owns the token can delete this task: its creator, its assignee or an account admin with a token that reaches account administration (an API key, or OAuth with the `admin` scope).

can_edit.description: Whether the user who owns the token can edit, complete or reopen this task.

companies.description: The companies the task is linked to. Empty when it has none.

iri.description: IRI of the record; send it in the same field to link it.

label.description: Name of the record: the full name of a contact, the name of a company or opportunity.

secondary.description: Second line that tells records with the same name apart: the email of a contact, the primary domain of a company. `null` when there is none.

completed_at.description: When the task was completed. `null` while it is open.

completed_by.description: Who completed the task. `null` while it is open.

kind.description: Kind of actor: `user` for a person, otherwise `contact`, `automation`, `integration`, `system` or `external`.

name.description: Name of the actor. `null` when the person is no longer a member of the account.

contacts.description: The contacts the task is linked to. Empty when it has none.

iri.description: IRI of the record; send it in the same field to link it.

label.description: Name of the record: the full name of a contact, the name of a company or opportunity.

secondary.description: Second line that tells records with the same name apart: the email of a contact, the primary domain of a company. `null` when there is none.

created_at.description: When the task was created, ISO 8601.

created_by.description: Who decided to create the task. `null` when the creator is unknown. It is not the assignee.

kind.description: Kind of actor: `user` for a person, otherwise `contact`, `automation`, `integration`, `system` or `external`.

name.description: Name of the actor. `null` when the person is no longer a member of the account.

description_html.description: Longer description as limited HTML (paragraphs, line breaks, bold, italic and links). `null` when there is none.

due_at.description: When the task is due, ISO 8601 with the time zone offset (the instant is stored in UTC). `null` when it has no due date.

initiated_via.description: How the task was created: `ui` (the app), `maia`, `api`, `import`, `sync`, `automation` or `system`.

opportunities.description: The opportunities the task is linked to. Empty when it has none.

iri.description: IRI of the record; send it in the same field to link it.

label.description: Name of the record: the full name of a contact, the name of a company or opportunity.

secondary.description: Second line that tells records with the same name apart: the email of a contact, the primary domain of a company. `null` when there is none.

overdue.description: `true` when the task is open and its due date has passed. Always `false` for a completed task. It is calculated when you read it.

reminder_at.description: Instant of the reminder, calculated from `due_at` and `reminder_offset_minutes`. Read-only. `null` when there is no reminder.

reminder_offset_minutes.description: Minutes before `due_at` at which the assignee is reminded; `0` means at the due time. `null` when there is no reminder.

status.description: `open` while the task is pending, `completed` once it is done.

title.example: Send the revised proposal to Ana

type.description: Kind of work. It only classifies the task: completing a `call` or `email` task does not make a call or send an email.

updated_at.description: When the task last changed, ISO 8601.

uuid.description: UUID of the task.

version.description: Version of the task; it grows with every change. Send it as `expected_version` to make sure nobody changed the task in between.

WebhookEventType.description:
Webhook event types:
* `member_subscribed` - triggered when a member subscribes to an audience
* `member_unsubscribed` - triggered when a member unsubscribes from an audience
* `member_added_to_group` - triggered when a member is added to a group
* `member_removed_from_group` - triggered when a member is removed from a group
* `member_campaign_opened` - triggered when a member opens a campaign
* `member_campaign_clicked` - triggered when a member clicks a link in a campaign
* `member_campaign_delivered` - triggered when a campaign email is delivered
* `member_campaign_bounced` - triggered when a member's email address bounces
* `member_campaign_complained` - triggered when a member reports a campaign as spam
* `member_automation_started` - triggered when a member starts an automation
* `member_automation_completed` - triggered when a member completes an automation
* `member_automation_cancelled` - triggered when a member cancels an automation
* `custom_automation_step` - triggered by a Send Webhook automation step
* `member_sms_subscribed` - triggered when a contact opts in to SMS
* `member_sms_unsubscribed` - triggered when a contact opts out of SMS
* `member_sms_delivered` - triggered when an SMS is delivered
* `member_sms_bounced` - triggered when an SMS hard-bounces (failed delivery)
* `member_sms_clicked` - triggered when a member clicks a link in an SMS campaign
* `member_sms_replied` - triggered when a contact replies to an SMS campaign

info.description:
The Easymailing API provides a comprehensive set of RESTful endpoints that allow you to programmatically manage campaigns, audiences, subscribers, statistics, and more.  
Built around REST principles, the API features predictable resource-oriented URLs, standard HTTP response codes, and commonly used methods such as GET, POST, PUT, and DELETE.  
This documentation outlines all available REST API methods, complete with example requests and responses. Additionally, you can import this documentation into tools like Postman to test and interact with the API using your personal authentication token.  

If you need additional functionality that the API doesn't currently support, please [contact us](https://ayuda.easymailing.com).

### Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS)  
The Easymailing API is designed to be accessed from server-side applications only. Client-side requests are not permitted.  

### Authentication  
The Easymailing API supports two authentication methods:

#### Option 1: API Key (recommended for direct integrations)  
API keys are the quickest way to implement machine-to-machine authentication. Use this method when building your own integrations with Easymailing.  
- Use the `X-Auth-Token` header to provide your API key in each request.  
- You can generate your API key in the Easymailing control panel under **Config > API Keys**.  

Example request:  
```bash
curl -X GET 'https://api.easymailing.com/my_suscription' \
     --header 'Content-Type: application/ld+json' \
     --header 'X-Auth-Token: <YOUR_API_KEY>'
```

#### Option 2: OAuth2 Bearer Token (for third-party apps)  
If you are building a third-party application that connects to Easymailing on behalf of users, use OAuth2 authentication. Users authorize your app through the OAuth2 flow, and your app receives an access token to make API requests on their behalf.  
- Use the `Authorization` header with the Bearer token.  
- Refer to our [OAuth2 documentation](https://developers.easymailing.com/oauth) for details on implementing the authorization flow.  

Example request:  
```bash
curl -X GET 'https://api.easymailing.com/my_suscription' \
     --header 'Content-Type: application/ld+json' \
     --header 'Authorization: Bearer <ACCESS_TOKEN>'
```

get.description:
Returns the background tasks of the account, newest first, each with its type, status and progress. A task is created when you call one of the asynchronous operations on groups and segments (for example `async_task_group_export` or `async_task_segment_add_to_group`).

**When to use:** To find a task whose UUID you did not keep, or to see what is still running.

**When not to use:** To follow one task whose UUID you know use `get_async_task`.

**Permissions:** Requires the viewer role or higher, or the `marketing.audiences.read` capability.

401.description: Missing, invalid, expired or deactivated credentials, or the account is not active, suspended or expired. An unknown API key or token answers `{"message": …}` as `application/json`; the other cases are problem+json with the reason in `detail`.

403.description: The credential is not allowed to do this (see Permissions). Use a key or token with a higher role or the required capability.

429.description: Too many requests with the same API key (a fixed window of one minute). `Retry-After` says when to try again.

Retry-After.description: Moment from which to retry, as `Y-m-d H:i:s` in the server time zone (not seconds).

X-RateLimit-Remaining.description: Requests left in the current window.

get.description:
Returns the state of one background task: its status, how many items were processed or failed, the progress and, if it failed, the error. For exports it also gives a temporary address (valid 15 minutes) to download the file.

**When to use:** After calling an asynchronous operation (those whose `operationId` starts with `async_task_`): it returns a task at once, not the result. Starts a background job that adds to the group the members of the audience that match your conditions. Members already in the group should be skipped (see side effects). It runs in the background and returns an async task straight away, not the final result: read it with `get_async_task` using the task `uuid` and repeat until `status` is `completed` or `failed`.

**When to use:** To fill a group from a one-off rule, for example everyone in Spain who opened a campaign, without creating a saved segment.

**When not to use:** To add one member, use `member_add_from_group`. To reuse a saved segment, use `async_task_segment_add_to_group`. To remove members, use `async_task_group_remove_from_conditions`.

**Side effects:** Starts an async task. For each member added it records an entry in the member's activity and fires the automations triggered by joining a group; the group's member count is refreshed. It does not fire the `member_added_to_group` webhook. A member who is already in this group but also in another group is selected again: their activity entry and group automations can run a second time, and they are counted in `result_meta.added`. Each condition has a `field` (IRI of a condition field from `list_audience_condition_fields`), an `operator` (one of the `operators` that field lists) and a `value` whose type depends on the field: text, integer, decimal, boolean, date string (`2026-01-15`) or an array for multi-select fields.

**Permissions:** Requires the manager role or higher, or the `marketing.audiences.write` capability.

post.description:
Starts a background job that unsubscribes the email and the SMS channel of the members of the segment that are confirmed. It runs in the background and returns an async task straight away, not the final result: read it with `get_async_task` using the task `uuid` and repeat until `status` is `completed` or `failed`. It is NOT the bulk version of `member_unsubscribe`: it writes the new status directly.

**When to use:** To stop sending to a whole slice of an audience at once, for example inactive contacts.

**When not to use:** For a single member, use `member_unsubscribe`, which also fires the unsubscription webhook and cancels the member's automations. To delete the people instead of unsubscribing them, use `async_task_segment_delete_contacts`.

**Side effects:** Starts an async task. The affected members change to `suscriber.status.unsuscribed.admin` (email) and their SMS status to the same value, they stop receiving campaigns, and the unsubscription is recorded in the activity of each email-unsubscribed member. Unlike `member_unsubscribe` it does NOT fire the `member_unsubscribed` / `member_sms_unsubscribed` webhooks and does NOT cancel the automations the members are in. The audience statistics are refreshed afterwards. `result_meta.unsubscribed` counts only the members whose email status was confirmed. Channels that are not confirmed are left as they are. If no member of the segment has a confirmed email, the job ends without changing anyone, even if some have a confirmed SMS.

**Permissions:** Requires the manager role or higher, or the `marketing.audiences.write` capability.

get.description:
Lists the members of one audience, most recently updated first, with their status, groups, custom field values and engagement stats. A member is one person's subscription to this audience. Each member carries its `contact`, the IRI of the person.

**When to use:** To browse or export the people of an audience, or to find members by status, source, group or form. To look a person up by email in this audience, filter with `email`.

**When not to use:** To find out in which audiences a person is, whatever the audience, use `search_member`. To read one member whose UUID you know, use `get_audience_member`. To list the people of the account whatever their audiences, with their company, tags and attributes, use `list_contacts`.

**Filters:**
All filters are optional and combine with AND.
- `email`: partial match on the email address.
- `phone`: exact match, E.164.
- `status` / `sms_status`: exact subscription status of the email / SMS channel.
- `source` and `email_opt_in_source`: how the member entered the audience (both filter the same column).
- `sms_opt_in_source`: how the member opted in to SMS.
- `groups`: comma-separated group UUIDs; only members in all of them.
- `suscription_form`: members who signed up through that form.
Sorting: `order[field]=asc|desc` with `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `status`, `source`, `contact.email`, `uniqueOpens`, `uniqueClicks`, `deliveredEmails`, `orders`, `revenue` or `rating`. Default: `updatedAt` descending.

**Permissions:** Requires the manager role or higher, or the `contacts.read` and `marketing.audiences.read` capabilities.

post.description:
Adds a person to an audience and requests their email subscription, or merges the data you send into the member if that person is already in the audience. People are matched across the whole account by email, then by phone, so the same person is one contact with one member per audience. The response includes the `contact` IRI of the person.

**When to use:** To subscribe a new person or re-send a sign-up from a form, store or integration. It is safe to call again for the same email. Members are also created by `create_store_customer` (shop buyers) and by the public subscription forms.

**When not to use:** To create a person without subscribing them to any audience, use `create_contact`. To subscribe a contact you already have by UUID, use `subscribe_contact_to_audience`. To change data of a member you already have by UUID, use `update_audience_member`. To subscribe an existing member again use `member_subscribe`; to unsubscribe one use `member_unsubscribe`. To see in which audiences an email already is, use `search_member`. To register a shop buyer together with their customer record, use `create_store_customer`.

**Side effects:** What the person receives depends on their state. A new person (or one still unconfirmed) in a double opt-in audience gets a confirmation email and stays `suscriber.status.unconfirmed` until they confirm, unless `disable_double_opt_in=true`. In a single opt-in audience, or with `disable_double_opt_in=true`, they become `suscriber.status.confirmed` at once: the `member_subscribed` webhook fires, automations triggered by a subscription start, and the welcome email is sent if the audience has one (unless `disable_welcome_email=true`). An email on the audience's suppression list always gets a confirmation email instead. Someone who unsubscribed on their own (`suscriber.status.unsuscribed`) is not subscribed again: they get a confirmation email and stay unsubscribed until they confirm, even with `disable_double_opt_in=true`. Someone whose status is `suscriber.status.unsuscribed.admin` (unsubscribed through the API, by an administrator or by the cleaning rules) can be subscribed again normally: in a single opt-in audience, or with `disable_double_opt_in=true`, this call confirms them again at once unless their address is on the suppression list. Do not use it to bring back a person who asked to leave. An already confirmed member only gets their data updated. Confirmation emails are not repeated within 15 minutes. If a phone is sent, the SMS subscription follows the audience's SMS opt-in (a confirmation SMS in double opt-in, unless `disable_sms_double_opt_in=true`). Groups assigned fire the `member_added_to_group` webhook and group automations once the member is confirmed.

**Permissions:** Requires the manager role or higher, or the `contacts.write` and `marketing.audiences.write` capabilities.

Changes the contact data, groups, custom field values or consent of an existing member. Fields you leave out keep their value. WARNING: changing the `email` or the `phone` to a different value resets the subscription of that channel for the whole person, in EVERY audience they belong to, not only this one: their email `status` (or `sms_status`) becomes empty, so they stop being a confirmed recipient everywhere until each of their members is subscribed again. Any other field leaves the subscription status as it is.

**When to use:** To correct or complete the data of a member identified by UUID: name, location, custom fields or groups. Change the email or phone only when the user explicitly asks for it, after telling them that the person will have to be subscribed again in all their audiences.

**When not to use:** To subscribe or unsubscribe someone, use `member_subscribe` or `member_unsubscribe`. To add or remove one group without resending the whole list, use `member_add_from_group` or `member_remove_from_group`. To add a new person, use `create_audience_member`. There is no way to change the email and keep the person subscribed: afterwards the person has to be subscribed again with `member_subscribe`. The name, email, phone and location edited here belong to the person's contact and are shared by all their audiences; the same data can also be changed with `update_contact`, which additionally handles company, owner, tags and attributes.

**Side effects:** If `email` or `phone` really changes (a different address, ignoring case, or a different number): in every audience of the person, the email `status` (for `email`) or `sms_status` (for `phone`) is set to empty, and the consent recorded for that channel is invalidated. No confirmation message is sent to the new address or number, so the person is not subscribed again until you call `member_subscribe` on each audience (it may not be able to do it, see that operation). Groups the member enters or leaves because of the new `groups` list fire the `member_added_to_group` and `member_removed_from_group` webhooks and the group automations.

**Permissions:** Requires the manager role or higher, or the `contacts.write` and `marketing.audiences.write` capabilities.

put.description:
Asks to subscribe again the email channel, the SMS channel or both of a member who already exists in the audience. It is a request, not a guarantee: the channel is confirmed at once only in some cases (see side effects); otherwise the person gets a confirmation message and the status does not change until they confirm.

**When to use:** When a person who never confirmed, or who was unsubscribed through `member_unsubscribe` or after changing their email or phone, asks to receive messages again and you have their member UUID. Check the `status` and `sms_status` in the response: they tell what really happened.

**When not to use:** To add someone who is not in the audience yet, use `create_audience_member`. To unsubscribe, use `member_unsubscribe`. Never use it to override a person who unsubscribed themselves: in that case it only sends them a confirmation email. If you have the contact UUID instead of the member UUID, `subscribe_contact_to_audience` does the same.

**Side effects:** Email channel. In a double opt-in audience the person always gets a confirmation email and the status changes only when they confirm. In a single opt-in audience the email is confirmed at once, except when the person unsubscribed themselves (`suscriber.status.unsuscribed`) or the address is on the audience's suppression list: then they get a confirmation email and stay as they were until they confirm. Confirmation emails are not repeated within 15 minutes. SMS channel: in an audience with SMS double opt-in the status becomes `suscriber.status.unconfirmed` and a confirmation SMS is sent; otherwise it is confirmed at once. When a channel is confirmed at once, the `member_subscribed` or `member_sms_subscribed` webhook fires, the automations triggered by a subscription start and, for email, the audience's welcome email is sent if it has one. A channel the person has no email or phone for is ignored. A channel whose consent was recorded by the new Customer App (this includes a channel invalidated by changing the email or phone) is left as it is and the call still answers 200: always read `status` and `sms_status` in the response. The `disable_double_opt_in` and `disable_welcome_email` flags of member creation do not apply here.

**Permissions:** Requires the manager role or higher, or the `contacts.write` and `marketing.audiences.write` capabilities.

put.description:
Unsubscribes the confirmed email channel, SMS channel or both of one member of this audience. The member keeps their record, groups and history, but stops receiving campaigns and automations from this audience. Only channels that are currently confirmed change.

**When to use:** When a person asks to stop receiving messages, or when the user wants to stop sending to one person without deleting them.

**When not to use:** To delete the person from the audience, use `delete_audience_member`. To subscribe them again, use `member_subscribe`. For many members of a segment there is `async_task_segment_unsubscribe`, but it is NOT the bulk version of this operation: it changes the status directly, without webhook, without cancelling automations and without the other effects listed here. If you have the contact UUID instead of the member UUID, `unsubscribe_contact_from_audience` does the same.

**Side effects:** Email: the status becomes `suscriber.status.unsuscribed.admin`, the unsubscription is recorded in the member's activity, the automations the member is in are cancelled (`member_automation_cancelled` webhook) and the `member_unsubscribed` webhook fires. SMS: the status becomes `suscriber.status.unsuscribed.admin` and the `member_sms_unsubscribed` webhook fires (automations are not cancelled for an SMS-only unsubscription). The address is not added to the audience's suppression list, so `create_audience_member` or `member_subscribe` can bring the person back in a single opt-in audience without a confirmation.

**Permissions:** Requires the manager role or higher, or the `contacts.write` and `marketing.audiences.write` capabilities.

post.description:
Splits the flow in two: the contact is checked against the conditions you define and goes down the "yes" branch if it meets them (all of them, or any of them) and down the "no" branch if not. Its place in the flow is set with `parent`, `parent_yes` or `parent_no`; with none of them it becomes the first step.

**When to use:** To treat contacts differently inside a flow: send another email to those who live in a given city, or skip an offer for those already in a group.

**When not to use:** A condition only splits the flow. To wait, use `create_step_delay`; to change the contact's data, use `create_step_update_custom_field`.

**Side effects:** The check happens when the contact reaches the step, with its data at that moment. The conditions are stored as an internal segment of the audience that does not appear in the segments list. Steps that follow go in a branch: place them with `parent_yes` or `parent_no` of this step, because `parent` cannot point to a condition step. If the chosen position is already occupied, the new step is inserted there and the step that was there moves into its "yes" branch.

**Permissions:** Requires the author role or higher, or the `marketing.automations.write` capability.

post.description:
Holds the contact before it moves to the next step, either for a relative amount of time (minutes, hours, days or weeks) or until a fixed moment: a time of day, certain weekdays, a day of the month or a calendar date. Its place in the flow is set with `parent`, `parent_yes` or `parent_no`; with none of them it becomes the first step.

**When to use:** Between steps of a flow: wait two days after a welcome email before the follow-up, or hold the next message until 9:00 the next morning.

**When not to use:** To branch on what the contact did, use `create_step_condition`; a delay only waits.

**Side effects:** The wait starts when the contact reaches the step. Time is counted in the contact's time zone, or in the audience's if the contact has none, or in UTC. A time-of-day wait ends at the next occurrence of that time, and a calendar date that has already passed lets the contact continue at once. Known issue: `day_week` is saved as the numbers you send (0 = Sunday), but the engine that resumes the contact reads weekday names, so a contact that reaches a `specific_day_week` wait may get stuck there; use another unit for now. If the chosen position is already occupied, the new step is inserted there and the step that was there moves after it.

**Permissions:** Requires the author role or higher, or the `marketing.automations.write` capability.

Its place in the flow is set with `parent`, `parent_yes` or `parent_no`; with none of them it becomes the first step.

**When to use:** To remove contacts who answered "stop", who asked to leave, or at the end of a sunset flow for inactive contacts.

**When not to use:** To only take a contact out of a group, use `create_step_remove_from_group`. To unsubscribe one contact outside any flow, use `member_unsubscribe`; to unsubscribe a segment, `async_task_segment_unsubscribe`.

**Side effects:** The contact is marked as unsubscribed by an administrator on the channels where it was subscribed and stops receiving the audience's messages there; its other automation runs in this audience are cancelled, and the matching unsubscribed webhook (`member_unsubscribed` for email) fires. If the chosen position is already occupied, the new step is inserted there and the step that was there moves after it.

**Permissions:** Requires the author role or higher, or the `marketing.automations.write` capability.

delete.description:
Deletes a step from the flow. By default the steps that followed it are reconnected to its parent so the flow stays connected; with `mode` set to cascade, the step and everything after it are deleted.

**When to use:** To remove one action from a flow, for example an email that is no longer wanted.

**When not to use:** To move a step instead of removing it, use `move_step_position`.

**Side effects:** Deleting a condition step in the default mode keeps only its "yes" branch and deletes the "no" branch. Any `mode` value other than `reconnect` is treated as `cascade`, which deletes the step and everything after it, so check the value before sending. It cannot be undone.

**Permissions:** Requires the author role or higher, or the `marketing.automations.write` capability.

post.description:
Starts the automation for a shopper whose cart in a store has not been modified for the chosen waiting time, optionally only when the cart contains (or, with `exclude`, does not contain) certain products or categories.

**When to use:** To send a cart-recovery email or SMS to shoppers who added products to a cart and never placed the order.

**When not to use:** For an order that was placed but not paid, use `create_trigger_payment_reminder`. To react when an order is paid, use `create_trigger_order_paid` (or `create_trigger_buy_a_product` for certain products). For a message weeks after buying, use `create_trigger_time_since_last_purchase`.

**Side effects:** Known limit: the scheduled check only looks at carts last modified within the previous 2 hours, so a waiting time above 2 hours matches no cart and the trigger never fires; the wait counts from the cart's last change, not from its creation. The run is cancelled automatically if the order is processed or paid first. The cart is attached to the run so emails can use its data, and it must belong to a customer linked to a contact of the audience. Works only while the automation is active and the trigger is enabled, and only for contacts with a confirmed subscription. A contact that is already running through the automation is not started again; after finishing, it can enter again only if `workflow_repeat` is true and 24 hours have passed.

**Permissions:** Requires the author role or higher, or the `marketing.automations.write` capability.

Works only while the automation is active and the trigger is enabled, and only for contacts with a confirmed subscription. A contact is never started again within 6 months of its previous run, and enters again at all only if `workflow_repeat` is true.

**When to use:** To chain a follow-up to a campaign: for example add everyone who received it to a group, or wait and send a second email.

**When not to use:** To react to what the contact does with the campaign, use `create_trigger_open_on_campaign` or `create_trigger_click_on_campaign`.

**Side effects:** It fires for every recipient as the campaign is sent, when the message is handed to the mail server and before delivery is known, so contacts whose message later bounces start it too. Works only while the automation is active and the trigger is enabled, and only for contacts with a confirmed subscription. A contact that is already running through the automation is not started again; after finishing, it can enter again only if `workflow_repeat` is true and 24 hours have passed.

delete.description:
Permanently removes a trigger. The automation stops starting from that event.

**When to use:** When an automation should no longer start that way, or to replace a trigger by one of another type: delete it and create the new one.

**When not to use:** To stop it only for a while, use `automation_trigger_pause`. To delete the whole automation, use `delete_automation`.

**Side effects:** The runs of contacts that entered through this trigger are deleted with it, so they disappear from the automation counters and from `list_automation_queues`. Because their runs disappear, those contacts are also forgotten by the "each contact runs once" rule of the automation.

**Permissions:** Requires the author role or higher, or the `marketing.automations.write` capability.

post.description:
Queues up to 500 API calls to be run one after another in the background, in the order given. It returns the batch at once; the calls run later. A call that fails does not stop the others.

Each call has `method` (POST, PUT, GET or DELETE), `path` (an endpoint of this API, for example `/audiences/{audienceUuid}/members`), an optional `body` (a JSON string), optional `params` (query parameters) and an optional `external_identifier` of yours to match results.

Each call is checked with the permissions of the token that created the batch, as if you sent it yourself: a call the token is not allowed to make is not run and shows a 403 in the results. The batch can therefore do anything those permissions allow, including deleting or sending.

The batch belongs to the user of the credential that creates it: only that user and an account administrator can read or delete it afterwards.

**When to use:** To load or change many records in one go, for example adding thousands of members or moving many members to groups, without waiting for each call.

**When not to use:** For one call, use the operation directly. To act on all members of a segment or group, use the asynchronous operations of Segments and Groups.

**Side effects:** Every call runs and takes effect in the background, with all the side effects of that operation (emails, automations, webhooks). A call that answers with a server error (500) is attempted up to 3 times. The calls run later with the credential that created the batch: if its user is deactivated before they run, the calls still pending fail with 401.

**Permissions:** No specific permission.

get.description:
Returns the email campaigns of your account, newest first, with their status (draft, scheduled, sending, sent...), type, audience and configuration. SMS campaigns are not included: they have their own list.

**When to use:** To find a campaign by name, status, type or audience, to see what was sent last, or to get the UUID that the other campaign operations ask for.

**When not to use:** To read one campaign in full, with its recipient count and delivery warnings, use `get_campaign`. For SMS campaigns, use `list_sms_campaigns`.

**Filters:** Default order: newest created first.

- `title`: campaigns whose name contains the text.
- `status`: exact status, for example `campaign.status.sent` (same values as the `status` field).
- `type`: exact type, for example `campaign.regular` or `campaign.test.ab` (same values as the `type` field). Automation campaigns (`campaign.automation`) are listed too.
- `hash`: exact hash of the campaign, the code that follows `em_ch=` in the links of its emails.
- `audience`: UUID of the audience.

Sorting: `order[createdAt]`, `order[updatedAt]`, `order[status]`, `order[startedAt]` (when sending began) or `order[finishedAt]` (when it ended), each `asc` or `desc`. The newest created campaign is not always the last one sent: for the last sent, combine `status=campaign.status.sent` with `order[startedAt]=desc&itemsPerPage=1`.

**Permissions:** Requires the viewer role or higher, or the `marketing.campaigns.read` capability.

**When not to use:** For an A/B test use `create_campaign_test_ab_subject`, `create_campaign_test_ab_sender` or `create_campaign_test_ab_template`. Creates a draft email campaign that asks subscribers to confirm they still want to receive your emails. Nothing is sent when you create it. Once it is sent, recipients who do not click the confirmation link end up unsubscribed. The template must contain the confirmation link tag `link.list.revalidation_confirm_subscription`. SCHEDULES THE CAMPAIGN FOR REAL: sets the date and time at which it will be sent to all its recipients, with no further action. Nothing goes out now; at that time the same real send as `campaign_send_now` happens, to real people, and it cannot be recalled. Before sending, check with `get_campaign` that the campaign has recipients (`recipient_count` above 0), no entry in `warnings` has `blocks_sending: true`, and its status is draft, ready or scheduled. The API does not check recipients, credits or account status when scheduling: they are checked when the scheduled time arrives, and if the check fails the campaign moves to `campaign.status.error` and nothing is sent.

**When to use:** Only when the person has confirmed the campaign and the date at which it must go out to all its recipients.

**When not to use:** To send right away, use `campaign_send_now`. To cancel the schedule, use `campaign_unschedule`. To check the email first, use `campaign_send_test`. For an SMS campaign, use `schedule_sms_campaign`. Automation campaigns cannot be scheduled.

**Side effects:** The status becomes `campaign.status.scheduled` and the send is queued for the date. At that time real emails go out and email credits are used. Until then the campaign can be edited with `update_campaign` or cancelled with `campaign_unschedule`. Scheduling an already scheduled campaign replaces its date. With `campaign_confirmation_email`, a confirmation email goes to `mailing_confirm_emails` when the sending ends.

**Permissions:** Requires the manager role or higher, or the `marketing.campaigns.send` capability.

put.description:
SENDS THE CAMPAIGN FOR REAL: starts delivering the email right away to every recipient of the campaign. These are real emails to real people; once it starts it cannot be undone or recalled. Before sending, check with `get_campaign` that the campaign has recipients (`recipient_count` above 0), no entry in `warnings` has `blocks_sending: true`, and its status is draft, ready or scheduled. The checks run at the moment of sending, not before: if one fails the request is rejected.

**When to use:** Only when the person has confirmed that this campaign must go out now to all its recipients.

**When not to use:** To send at a later time, use `campaign_schedule`. To see how the email looks, use `campaign_send_test`: it sends only to the addresses you list. For an SMS campaign, use `send_sms_campaign_now`. Automation campaigns cannot be sent manually.

**Side effects:** Real delivery: the status becomes `campaign.status.sending` and then `campaign.status.sent`, the sends use email credits of the plan and count against the daily sending limit, and opens, clicks and bounces start to be recorded. A scheduled campaign can also be sent now; its schedule is cancelled. With `campaign_confirmation_email`, a confirmation email goes to `mailing_confirm_emails` when the sending ends. If a check at send time fails (no active subscribers, account not allowed to send, not enough credits, daily limit reached, expired subscription, no content, blocked audience), the request returns 400 and the campaign is left in `campaign.status.error`: it can no longer be edited or sent, so retry with a copy from `duplicate_campaign`.

**Permissions:** Requires the manager role or higher, or the `marketing.campaigns.send` capability.
