Lists the companies of the account, most recently changed first, with their domains, owner, location, classification and number of linked contacts. A company is an organization your contacts work for; it is shared by the whole account and is not tied to any audience.

**When to use:** To browse companies or to find one by name, domain, owner, country or industry before reading, editing or linking it to a contact.

**When not to use:** To read one company whose UUID you know, use `get_company`. To list the people of a company, use `list_contacts` with the `company` filter. To find people rather than organizations, use `list_contacts`. This list does not return description, social links, phones or attributes; `get_company` does.

**Filters:** All filters are optional and combine with AND.
- `name`: partial match, case-insensitive.
- `domain`: exact match on any domain of the company, written as in `domains` (`acme.com`).
- `owner`: email of the owner user.
- `country_code`: exact two-letter country code.
- `city`: partial match.
- `company_type`: exact value (`private`, `public`...).
- `industry`: an industry of `list_company_industries`, as its UUID or exact label.
- `record_source`: exact value (`api`, `import`, `connected_mailbox`...).
Sorting: `order[field]=asc|desc` with `name`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `employees`, `annual_revenue` or `founded_year`. Default: `updated_at` descending (up to 4 `order` fields).
Pagination: `page` and `itemsPerPage`, like the rest of the API; the response gives the total in `hydra:totalItems`.

**Permissions:** Requires a CRM seat and the `crm.contacts_companies.read` capability.

Creates a company in the CRM, standalone: it is not linked to any contact or audience. Every editable field (domains, owner, location, classification, social links and attribute values) can be sent in the same request, and they are all saved together or not at all. The company is recorded as created through the API.

**When to use:** To register an organization the account does not have yet, before or after creating the people who work for it.

**When not to use:** To add a person, use `create_contact`; that operation can also link the person to a company. Before creating, check that the company does not exist: search by domain with `list_companies`, because a domain can belong to only one company. To change an existing company, use `update_company`.

**Side effects:** The company appears in the CRM with a `created` entry in its activity, attributed to the person who owns the token, with the note "via Maia" when Maia made the call. It is not linked to any contact: link a contact to it with `update_contact`. Nothing is sent and no automation or webhook fires (CRM webhook events do not exist yet).

**Permissions:** Requires a CRM seat and the `crm.contacts_companies.write` capability.

delete.description:
Permanently deletes a company. Its contacts and opportunities stay, no longer linked to it. There is no archive and no undo.

**When to use:** Only when the user explicitly asks to delete this company for good, for example a duplicate or a test record.

**When not to use:** To fix a wrong name, domain or owner, use `update_company`. To detach a person from the company without deleting it, use `update_contact` with `company` set to `null`. There is no merge of companies: to consolidate duplicates, move the contacts with `update_contact`, then delete the duplicate.

**Side effects:** Deleted with the company: its activity, its notes, its files (a Google Drive reference never deletes the original in Drive) and its attribute values; its domains are freed. Kept but unlinked from it: contacts (each gets a `company unlinked` entry in its activity), opportunities (same), tasks and meetings; connected emails stay, no longer shown under the company. If the account creates companies automatically from connected Gmail or Calendar, a new email or meeting with one of its domains can create it again; there is no list of suppressed domains. No webhook fires.

**Permissions:** Requires a CRM seat and the `crm.companies.delete` capability.

post.description:
Defines a new custom attribute for companies, placed after the existing ones. Once created, it can be filled in on any company through its `public_code`. Its visual presentation (languages, help text, display style) is left at the defaults and can be tuned in the app.

**When to use:** When the account needs to store a new piece of data on organizations that the company does not already have, for example a market segment or a renewal date.

**When not to use:** To change an existing attribute, use `update_company_attribute`. To set a value on a company, use `update_company`: this operation only defines the field, it does not set any value.

**Side effects:** Records the creation in the account's attribute change log, under the person who made the call. No webhook is fired.

**Permissions:** Requires the `crm.companies.attributes.manage` capability.

put.description:
Changes the name, the description or the options of a company attribute. Fields left out stay as they are. Values already stored on companies are not touched; renaming an option or the attribute changes how they read, not what is stored.

**When to use:** To rename an attribute, add, rename, recolor, reorder or archive options of an `enum` or `multi_enum`, or edit the description.

**When not to use:** The `type`, the `public_code` and the `currency` cannot be changed: create a new attribute instead. To stop using the attribute altogether, use `archive_company_attribute`.

**Side effects:** Records the change in the account's attribute change log, under the person who made the call. No webhook is fired.

**Permissions:** Requires the `crm.companies.attributes.manage` capability.

put.description:
Archives a company attribute: it stops accepting new values, but the values already stored are kept and its public code stays reserved. It can be restored.

**When to use:** When an attribute is no longer used but its history must be kept. This is the way to retire an attribute.

**When not to use:** To bring it back, use `restore_company_attribute`. To remove only some options, use `update_company_attribute` and archive those options.

**Side effects:** Records the change in the account's attribute change log, under the person who made the call. No webhook is fired. Archiving is refused while saved views, segments, campaigns, automations or other items in the app depend on the attribute.

**Permissions:** Requires the `crm.companies.attributes.manage` capability.

get.description:
Returns the catalog of industries a company can have, with their UUID and label. The catalog is the same for every account and cannot be changed.

**When to use:** Before setting `industries` on `create_company` or `update_company`, or filtering `list_companies` by `industry`, to pick a valid value.

**When not to use:** To see the industries of one company, read it with `get_company`. To define your own classification for companies, create an `enum` attribute with `create_company_attribute`.

**Filters:** No filters. The whole catalog is returned in one response, sorted by label; it is not paginated.

**Permissions:** Requires a CRM seat and the `crm.contacts_companies.read` capability.

get.description:
Lists every custom attribute defined for contacts in the account, active and archived, ordered by position: name, type, public code, options and whether it is archived. The list is complete, not paginated, and has no filters.

**When to use:** Before reading or writing the `attributes` of a contact, to learn which attributes exist, their `public_code` (the key to use), their type and, for `enum` and `multi_enum`, the options a value can take. **When not to use:** To list the custom fields of an audience (data stored per member), use `list_audience_custom_fields`. To read the attributes of one contact, read the contact itself with `get_contact`; this operation lists definitions, not values.

**Filters:** None. Archived attributes are included: check `status` on each item.

**Permissions:** Requires the `contacts.read` capability.

post.description:
Creates a person in the account with their data, tags and attributes, and optionally links them to an existing company. The person is not added to any audience and no email is sent. It needs at least an email or a phone, and it never merges with an existing contact: if the email or phone already belongs to another person the call fails.

**When to use:** To register a person who is not a subscriber yet, for example a lead, a customer or someone you met, so you can work with them in the CRM.

**When not to use:** To subscribe a person to an audience, use `create_audience_member`: it creates the contact if it does not exist, matches it by email or phone if it does, and requests the subscription. To subscribe a contact you already have, use `subscribe_contact_to_audience`. To change a contact that already exists, use `update_contact`. To register a company, use `create_company`.

**Side effects:** The creation is recorded in the contact's activity as done by the person who owns the key or token (marked «via Maia» when Maia made the request), and the contact's `record_source` is `api`. The contact belongs to no audience, receives no email and is not subscribed to anything. Retrying a request that already succeeded fails with `contact_identity_conflict` because the email or phone now exists; it does not create a second person. Tags that do not exist yet are created.

**Permissions:** Requires the `contacts.read` and `contacts.write` capabilities. Sending `company` also requires a CRM seat and the `crm.contacts_companies.write` capability.

put.description:
Requests the subscription of an existing contact to an audience, on the email channel, the SMS channel or both, using the contact's current primary email and phone. If the person is not in the audience yet, the membership (the member) is created; if they already are, their subscription is requested again. It is a request, not a guarantee: the channel is confirmed at once only in some cases (see side effects); otherwise the person gets a confirmation message and stays unconfirmed until they confirm.

**When to use:** When you already have the contact and want it in an audience, or when someone who never confirmed, or was unsubscribed through the API, asks to receive messages again. Check `status` and `sms_status` in the response: they tell what really happened.

**When not to use:** To create the person and subscribe them in one call, use `create_audience_member`. To create a person without subscribing them, use `create_contact`. If you have the member UUID instead of the contact, `member_subscribe` does the same. Never use it to override a person who unsubscribed themselves: in that case it only sends them a confirmation email.

**Side effects:** It follows the legacy subscription rules of the audience. Email channel: in a double opt-in audience the person always gets a confirmation email and the status changes only when they confirm; in a single opt-in audience the email is confirmed at once, except when the person unsubscribed themselves (`suscriber.status.unsuscribed`) or the address is on the audience's suppression list: then they get a confirmation email and stay as they were until they confirm. Confirmation emails are not repeated within 15 minutes. SMS channel: in an audience with SMS double opt-in the status becomes `suscriber.status.unconfirmed` and a confirmation SMS is sent; otherwise it is confirmed at once. When a channel is confirmed at once, the `member_subscribed` or `member_sms_subscribed` webhook fires, the automations triggered by a subscription start and, for email, the audience's welcome email is sent if it has one. A channel the contact has no email or phone for is ignored. A channel whose consent was recorded by the new Customer App (this includes a channel invalidated by changing the email or phone) is left as it is and the call still answers 200: always read the statuses in the response. The `disable_*` flags apply only when the membership did not exist and is created by this call.

**Permissions:** Requires the `marketing.audiences.write` capability.

delete.description:
Permanently deletes a person from the account: their data, tags, attribute values, notes and files, their activity and their subscriptions to every audience. The company and the opportunities of the person survive without the link, tasks survive without the association, and email suppressions already recorded stay. It cannot be undone.

**When to use:** Only when the user explicitly asks to erase the person from the account for good.

**When not to use:** To stop sending emails to the person but keep their record, use `unsubscribe_contact_from_audience` or `member_unsubscribe`. To take the person out of one audience only, use `delete_contact_audience_membership`; removing the last membership never deletes the contact. This is not a legal data-erasure request process.

**Side effects:** The contact, its audience memberships (with their groups, custom field values and history), its attribute values, tags, notes, files and activity are deleted. Companies and opportunities are kept and lose the link; tasks are kept and lose the association with the contact; meetings and synced emails are kept and lose the link to the person. Suppressions already recorded stay and deleting does not add a new one. Aggregate statistics of past campaigns are kept without the personal link.

**Permissions:** Requires the `contacts.delete` capability.

put.description:
Changes the data of a person: name, email, phone, job title, location, links, owner, company, tags and attribute values. Fields you leave out keep their value. Changing the primary `email` or `phone` keeps the person subscribed: a contact is the person, so in every audience where that channel was confirmed it stays confirmed with the new address or number. Only a subscription still waiting for confirmation is reset (its confirmation message went to the old address and can no longer be completed), and unsubscribed channels stay unsubscribed.

**When to use:** To correct or complete the data of a person identified by UUID, to update their email or phone when they change it, to assign an owner, to link them to a company or to set tags and attributes.

**When not to use:** To subscribe or unsubscribe the person, use `subscribe_contact_to_audience` or `unsubscribe_contact_from_audience`. To change data that belongs to one audience (its groups or custom fields), use `update_audience_member`. To add a new person, use `create_contact`.

**Side effects:** All the fields of the request are applied together: if one is rejected, nothing is saved and the contact stays as it was. Every field that really changes is recorded in the contact's activity as done by the person who owns the key or token (marked «via Maia» when Maia made the request); sending the value a field already has records nothing. If the primary `email` or `phone` really changes, confirmed subscriptions of that channel keep their status with the new destination; a pending confirmation of that channel is cancelled and its status emptied; no message is sent to the new address or number. Tags that do not exist yet are created.

**Permissions:** Requires the `contacts.read` and `contacts.write` capabilities. Setting or removing `company` also requires a CRM seat and the `crm.contacts_companies.write` capability.

get.description:
Lists the notes written on one contact, company or opportunity, newest first, with their text, author and dates.

**When to use:** To read what has been written down about a record: previous calls, agreements, context before a meeting or a follow-up.

**When not to use:** You must name the record: there is no list of all the notes of the account. To read one note whose UUID you know, use `get_note`. For things that have to be done, with a due date and a person responsible, use `list_tasks`.

**Filters:** Exactly one of `contact`, `company` or `opportunity` is required, with the UUID of the record. A UUID that does not exist, or that the user cannot see, gives `404`. The order is fixed (newest first); there is no `order` parameter and no text search.
Pagination: notes are paged with `itemsPerPage` (default 30, maximum 50) and an opaque `cursor[gt]`: to read the next page, call again with the same record and the `cursor[gt]` of the `hydra:next` link of the previous response. The response gives the total number of notes of the record in `hydra:totalItems`; keep following `hydra:next` until a page comes back empty. `hydra:previous` takes you back: it carries the `cursor[lt]` of the first note of the page and returns the page just before it; use it the same way, with the same record.

**Permissions:** Requires a CRM seat and the `crm.tasks_notes.read` capability. The note is only visible to users who can see the record it belongs to: `crm.contacts_companies.read` for a contact or company, `crm.opportunities.read` plus access to the pipeline for an opportunity.

post.description:
Creates an opportunity (a deal) in a pipeline, optionally in a given stage and with amount, expected close date, company, contacts, owner and attribute values. Everything is saved together or not at all. It is recorded as created through the API.

**When to use:** To register a new deal for a company or contact, for example after a qualifying conversation.

**When not to use:** To change a deal that already exists, use `update_opportunity`; to move it between stages, `move_opportunity_stage`. Check first with `list_opportunities` (filters `company` and `contact`) that the deal does not exist, because nothing prevents duplicates. To add a person or an organization, use `create_contact` or `create_company`.

**Side effects:** The opportunity appears in the CRM with an `opportunity.created` entry in its activity, attributed to the person who owns the key or token, with the note «via Maia» when Maia made the call. Its `record_source` is `api`. If you send `owner`, that user gets the assignment notification (in-app and, by default, email) unless they are the caller. Nothing is sent to contacts, no automation runs and no webhook fires (CRM webhook events do not exist yet). Retrying a request that succeeded creates a second opportunity.

**Permissions:** Requires a CRM seat and the `crm.opportunities.work` capability. It also needs `work` access to the pipeline where it is created.

delete.description:
Permanently deletes an opportunity. There is no trash and no undo.

**When to use:** Only when the user explicitly asks to delete this deal for good, for example a duplicate or a test record.

**When not to use:** If the deal was lost or is no longer worth pursuing, close it with `lose_opportunity` so it stays in the reports. To fix a wrong title, amount or owner, use `update_opportunity`.

**Side effects:** Deleted with the opportunity: its activity, its notes, its files (a Google Drive reference never deletes the original in Drive) and its attribute values; the links to its company and contacts. Company and contacts stay. Tasks stay and lose the association with the opportunity; synced emails and meetings stay and lose the link to it. The owner's pending assignment notification is closed. No webhook fires.

**Permissions:** Requires a CRM seat and the `crm.pipelines.manage` capability. It also needs `admin` access to the pipeline of the opportunity.

put.description:
Changes the data of an existing opportunity: title, description, amount, probability override, expected close date, company, contacts, owner and attribute values. Properties you leave out keep their value; `null` clears an optional one. It does not change the stage or the pipeline.

**When to use:** To correct or complete a deal, change its amount or expected date, link a company or contacts, assign an owner or set attributes.

**When not to use:** To change the stage use `move_opportunity_stage`; to close it, `win_opportunity` or `lose_opportunity`; to reopen it, `reopen_opportunity`; to change its pipeline, `move_opportunity_pipeline`. **Side effects:** All properties of the request are applied together: if one is rejected, nothing is saved. Each field that really changes adds an `opportunity.fields_changed` entry to the activity (field, previous and new value), attributed to the person who owns the key or token, with the note «via Maia» when Maia made the call; saving the same value leaves no entry. Changing `value` of a won or lost deal revalues its closing snapshot. If it sets a new owner who is not the caller, that user gets the assignment notification (in-app and, by default, email); the previous owner's pending notification is closed. Nothing is sent and no automation or webhook fires.

**Permissions:** Requires a CRM seat and the `crm.opportunities.work` capability. It also needs `work` access to the pipeline of the opportunity.

Nothing is sent and no automation or webhook fires.

**Permissions:** Requires a CRM seat and the `crm.opportunities.work` capability. It also needs `work` access to the pipeline of the opportunity.

put.description:
Moves an opportunity to another stage of its pipeline. The move follows the stage type: entering a won or lost stage closes the deal, entering an open stage from a closed one reopens it.

**When to use:** To advance or move back a deal in its pipeline, for example from Qualified to Negotiation.

**When not to use:** To close a deal as won or lost, `win_opportunity` and `lose_opportunity` find the stage for you. To reopen a closed deal, use `reopen_opportunity`. To change the pipeline, use `move_opportunity_pipeline`. To change other data of the deal, use `update_opportunity`.

**Side effects:** Adds an `opportunity.stage_changed` entry to the activity (from stage, to stage and kind: progressed, won, lost, reopened), attributed to the person who owns the key or token, with the note «via Maia» when Maia made the call. The time in the previous stage is closed and a new stay starts. Entering a won stage sets probability 100, a lost stage 0, and the closing amount is valued at the closing date. Moving to the stage it is already in changes nothing. Nothing is sent and no automation or webhook fires.

**Permissions:** Requires a CRM seat and the `crm.opportunities.work` capability. It also needs `work` access to the pipeline of the opportunity.

put.description:

**When to use:** When a closed deal comes back to life, for example the customer returns after a loss or a win was registered by mistake.

The previous closing (date, amount snapshot and loss reason) stays in the history, a custom probability set before is not restored and a later close gets a new closing date. Nothing is sent and no automation or webhook fires.

**Permissions:** Requires a CRM seat and the `crm.opportunities.work` capability. It also needs `work` access to the pipeline of the opportunity.

put.description:
Closes an opportunity as won: it moves to the won stage of its pipeline, its probability becomes 100 and the closing date and the value of the sale are recorded.

**When to use:** When the user says the deal was closed successfully, signed or bought.

**When not to use:** To close it as lost, use `lose_opportunity`. To put it in an open stage, use `move_opportunity_stage`. To undo a mistaken win and keep working the deal, use `reopen_opportunity`.

**Side effects:** Same record as `move_opportunity_stage`: an `opportunity.stage_changed` entry with kind `won`, attributed to the person who owns the key or token, with the note «via Maia» when Maia made the call. If it was lost, it changes the outcome and keeps the first closing date. If it is already in that won stage, nothing changes. The closing amount is valued at the rate of the closing date; with no rate yet the value is marked `pending` and filled later. Nothing is sent and no automation or webhook fires.

**Permissions:** Requires a CRM seat and the `crm.opportunities.work` capability. It also needs `work` access to the pipeline of the opportunity.

post.description:
Defines a new custom attribute for opportunities, placed after the existing ones. It is shared by all pipelines. Once created, it can be filled in on any opportunity through its `public_code`. Its visual presentation (languages, help text, display style) is left at the defaults and can be tuned in the app.

**When to use:** When the account needs to store a new piece of data on deals that the opportunity does not already have, for example the lead source, the contract type or the competitor.

**When not to use:** To change an existing attribute, use `update_opportunity_attribute`. To set a value on an opportunity, use `update_opportunity`: this operation only defines the field, it does not set any value. To make a pipeline stage require it, edit the pipeline in the app.

**Side effects:** Records the creation in the account's attribute change log, under the person who made the call. No webhook is fired.

**Permissions:** Requires a CRM seat and the `crm.companies.attributes.manage` capability. It is the same capability that manages company attributes.

put.description:
Looks up the DNS records of a verified domain (DKIM, mail server, DMARC and, with `links_aligned`, tracking) and marks the domain as authenticated when they are all right. The response says which checks passed (`checks`) and the values found (`results`). If any check fails, the domain is marked as NOT authenticated, even if it was authenticated before.

**When to use:** After creating the DNS records at your DNS provider, to verify them. Call it again if a check fails and you have corrected the records; DNS changes can take time to propagate.

**When not to use:** If the domain is not verified yet, confirm the email first (`resend_sender_domain_verification`).

**Side effects:** Changes the state of the domain on every call. When all checks pass: the domain becomes authenticated and aligned, campaigns from its addresses are signed with the domain's own DKIM and, if `links_aligned` is set and the tracking records are right, the SSL certificate of the tracking domain is requested in the background. When a check fails: the domain stops being authenticated, so campaigns lose the domain's own DKIM signature and, in accounts that must authenticate to send large volumes, campaigns of 1000 recipients or more are flagged as not sendable. Senders created later on an authenticated domain are confirmed on creation; existing ones are not changed.

**Permissions:** Requires the manager role or higher, or the `account.integrations.manage` capability.

put.description:
SCHEDULES THE CAMPAIGN FOR REAL: sets the date and time at which the text message will be sent to all its recipients, with no further action. Nothing goes out now; at that time the same real send as `send_sms_campaign_now` happens, to real people, and it cannot be recalled. Before sending, check with `get_sms_campaign` that the campaign has recipients (`recipient_count` above 0), no entry in `warnings` has `blocks_sending: true` (for example not enough SMS credits), and its status is draft, ready or scheduled. The API does not check recipients, credits or account status when scheduling: they are checked when the scheduled time arrives, and if the check fails the campaign moves to `campaign.status.error` and nothing is sent.

**When to use:** Only when the person has confirmed the SMS campaign and the date at which it must go out to all its recipients.

**When not to use:** To send right away, use `send_sms_campaign_now`. To check the message first, use `send_sms_campaign_test`. For an email campaign, use `campaign_schedule`.

**Side effects:** The status becomes `campaign.status.scheduled` and the send is queued for the date. At that time real SMS go out and SMS credits are used. Until then the campaign can be edited with `update_sms_campaign`. Scheduling an already scheduled campaign replaces its date. There is no operation to cancel a scheduled SMS campaign: to stop it, delete it with `delete_sms_campaign`.

**Permissions:** Requires the manager role or higher, or the `marketing.campaigns.send` capability.

put.description:
SENDS THE CAMPAIGN FOR REAL: starts delivering the text message right away to every recipient of the campaign, meaning the contacts with a confirmed SMS subscription and a phone number. These are real SMS to real people; once it starts it cannot be undone or recalled. Before sending, check with `get_sms_campaign` that the campaign has recipients (`recipient_count` above 0), no entry in `warnings` has `blocks_sending: true` (for example not enough SMS credits), and its status is draft, ready or scheduled. The checks run at the moment of sending, not before: if one fails the request is rejected.

**When to use:** Only when the person has confirmed that this SMS campaign must go out now to all its recipients.

**When not to use:** To send at a later time, use `schedule_sms_campaign`. To see the message on a phone, use `send_sms_campaign_test`: it sends only to the numbers you list. For an email campaign, use `campaign_send_now`.

**Side effects:** Real delivery: the status becomes `campaign.status.sending` and then `campaign.status.sent`, and SMS credits of the plan are used as the messages go out. A scheduled campaign can also be sent now; its schedule is cancelled. If a check at send time fails (no recipients, account not allowed to send, not enough credits, daily limit reached, expired subscription, blocked audience), the request returns 400 and the campaign is left in `campaign.status.error`: it can no longer be edited or sent, so retry with a copy from `duplicate_sms_campaign`.

**Permissions:** Requires the manager role or higher, or the `marketing.campaigns.send` capability.

**When to use:** When the payment is confirmed. It is the step that counts revenue.

**When not to use:** For orders loaded from the past, without revenue tracking, use `import_order`.

The API does not check the current status of the order: calling it on an order in another status is accepted and fires the order paid automations and the activity entry again.

**Permissions:** Requires the manager role or higher, or the `marketing.audiences.write` capability.

get.description:
Lists CRM tasks with their status, due date, person responsible and the contacts, companies and opportunities they are linked to. With no filters it returns the open tasks assigned to the user who owns the token, the most urgent first (overdue ones on top).

**When to use:** To answer what is pending: the user's own tasks, overdue tasks, tasks due today or this week, the tasks of a teammate, unassigned tasks, or everything open on one contact, company or opportunity.

**When not to use:** To read one task whose UUID you know, use `get_task`. To read the notes of a record, use `list_notes`. To find a valid person to assign a task to, use `list_task_assignees`. There is no text search on tasks: narrow by person, record, date, priority or type and read `title`.

**Filters:** All filters are optional and combine with AND.
- `assignee`: `me` (the user who owns the token), `unassigned`, `all`, or the email of an active user of the account. Default: `me`, or `all` when you filter by `contact`, `company` or `opportunity`.
- `include_completed`: `false` (default) returns only open tasks; `true` returns open and completed tasks. There is no filter for completed tasks only: read `status`.
- `priority`, `type`: exact value.
- `due_from` (inclusive) and `due_to` (exclusive): bounds of `due_at`, ISO 8601 with a time zone. Tasks without a due date are left out when either one is sent.
- `contact`, `company`, `opportunity`: only tasks linked to that record, by its UUID. Send one at most. A UUID that does not exist, or that the user cannot see, gives `404`.
Overdue tasks: send `due_to` set to the current instant and leave `include_completed` out. Tasks due on a given day: `due_from` at the start of the day and `due_to` at the start of the next, in the user time zone.
Sorting: `sort=due` (default) puts overdue tasks first, then open tasks by due date, then open tasks without due date, then completed ones (most recently completed first); `priority` orders from `high` to `none` and then by due date; `title` is alphabetical, ignoring case. There is no sort direction.
Pagination: tasks are paged with `itemsPerPage` (default 30, maximum 50) and an opaque `cursor[gt]`: to read the next page, call again with the same filters and the `cursor[gt]` of the `hydra:next` link of the previous response. The total number of tasks is not returned. Keep following `hydra:next` until a page comes back empty. `hydra:previous` takes you back: it carries the `cursor[lt]` of the first task of the page and returns the page just before it; use it the same way, with the same filters.

**Permissions:** Requires a CRM seat and the `crm.tasks_notes.read` capability. A task linked to contacts or companies is only visible to users who also have `crm.contacts_companies.read`, and a task linked to an opportunity only to users who can see its pipeline; a task the user cannot fully see is treated as if it did not exist.

parameters.description: Tasks per page. Default 30, maximum 50.
parameters.name: itemsPerPage

parameters.description: Opaque cursor of the next page, taken from the `hydra:next` link of the previous response. Use it only with the same filters.
parameters.name: cursor[gt]

parameters.description: Opaque cursor of the previous page, taken from the `hydra:previous` link of the response. Use it only with the same filters. Do not send it together with `cursor[gt]`.

post.description:
Creates an open task with a title and, optionally, a description, priority, type, person responsible, due date, reminder and links to contacts, companies and opportunities.

**When to use:** To record something that has to be done: a follow-up call to a contact, a proposal to send, a renewal to review. Link it to the records it is about so it shows up on them.

**When not to use:** To write down information without a deadline or an action, such as what was said in a meeting, use `create_note`. To change a task that already exists, use `update_task`; to mark it done, `complete_task`.

**Side effects:** The task is created open and, if it is linked to records, a `task.created` entry appears in the activity of each of them, done by the person who owns the token (marked «via Maia» when Maia made the request; `initiated_via` says `api` or `maia`). A task without links leaves no entry. All fields are applied together: if one is rejected, nothing is saved. If the task is assigned to a user other than the one who owns the token, that user gets a notification (in the app and by email, according to their notification preferences). If a reminder is set, the assignee also gets a notification at `reminder_at`; it is delivered by the same notification system as the Customer App. Nothing is sent to the contacts and no automation or webhook fires (CRM webhook events do not exist yet).

**Permissions:** Requires a CRM seat and the `crm.tasks_notes.write` capability. The user must also be able to see every contact, company and opportunity the task is linked to (`crm.contacts_companies.read` for contacts and companies, access to the pipeline for opportunities).

delete.description:
Permanently deletes a task, open or completed. There is no archive and no undo.

**When to use:** Only when the user explicitly asks to delete this task, for example one created by mistake or a duplicate.

**When not to use:** If the work is finished, use `complete_task`: the task stays in the history of its records. To fix a title, date or assignee, use `update_task`.

**Side effects:** The task disappears from its records and from every list; the `task.created`, `task.completed` and `task.reopened` entries already in their activity stay, and no deletion entry is added. The assignee's pending assignment and reminder notices are withdrawn. No webhook fires.

**Permissions:** Requires a CRM seat and the `crm.tasks_notes.write` capability. The user must also be able to see every contact, company and opportunity the task is linked to (`crm.contacts_companies.read` for contacts and companies, access to the pipeline for opportunities). Only the creator of the task, its assignee or an account admin can delete it; an admin needs a token that reaches account administration (an API key, or OAuth with the `admin` scope) to delete tasks of other people.

tags.description: A contact is a person in the account: one record per person, identified by their email or phone, with or without audiences, company or opportunities. Contact data (name, company, tags, attributes) is kept once; the person's subscription to each audience is a membership of that contact, which the Audiences category also shows as a member.
tags.name: Contacts

tags.description: A company is an organization your contacts work for, with its own domains, owner, location and attributes. It is shared by the whole account and is not tied to any audience. A contact belongs to at most one company; a company can have many contacts. A domain belongs to only one company.
tags.name: Companies

tags.description: An opportunity is a potential sale: a deal with an amount, an expected close date, a company, contacts and an owner that moves through the stages of a pipeline until it is won or lost. Opportunities live in pipelines and inherit their access: a user sees, works or deletes an opportunity only with the matching access to its pipeline, besides the account capability. Opportunities are independent of audiences.
tags.name: Opportunities

tags.description: A pipeline is a sales process: an ordered list of stages (open, won and lost) that opportunities go through, with a reference currency, entry requirements per stage and the loss reasons offered when a deal is lost. Stages and loss reasons belong to one pipeline and are managed under it. Who can see or work a pipeline is set in the app; each user sees only the pipelines they have been granted.
tags.name: Pipelines

tags.description: A task is a to-do of the team: a title, an optional due date and an optional person responsible, which can be linked to any number of contacts, companies and opportunities. A task is open or completed; creating, completing and reopening it is recorded in the activity of every record it is linked to. A task with no links is visible to the whole account; a task linked to records is visible only to users who can see all of them. Tasks are not notes: a note is text kept on one record, with no deadline or person responsible.
tags.name: Tasks

tags.description: A note is free text kept on one contact, company or opportunity: what was said in a call, an agreement, context for the next conversation. It has an optional title, an author and a history of edits, and it appears in the activity of its record. A note belongs to exactly one record and is visible only to users who can see that record; only an account admin or its author can edit or delete it. A note has no due date or person responsible: for something to do, use a task.
tags.name: Notes

tags.description: Contact attributes are the custom fields you define for people in the CRM (customer tier, birthday, interests...). They belong to the contact itself, not to an audience: every audience sees the same value. Each attribute has a type and a stable `public_code`, which is the key used in the `attributes` object of a contact. Contact attributes are different from the custom fields of an audience, which store data on each member of that audience.
tags.name: Contact attributes

tags.description: Company attributes are the custom fields you define for organizations in the CRM (industry segment, contract renewal, annual budget...). Each attribute has a type and a stable `public_code`, which is the key used in the `attributes` object of a company.
tags.name: Company attributes

tags.description: Opportunity attributes are the custom fields you define for deals in the CRM (lead source, contract type, estimated budget...). They are defined once for the whole account, not per pipeline: every opportunity of every pipeline can use them, and a pipeline stage can require one before an opportunity may enter it. Each attribute has a type and a stable `public_code`, which is the key used in the `attributes` object of an opportunity.
tags.name: Opportunity attributes

tags.description: Audiences are the lists that hold your subscribers. Each audience has its own members, groups, segments and custom fields, plus sending defaults: sender, double opt-in and GDPR.
tags.name: Audiences

tags.description: A member is one person's subscription to one audience. The same person (same email or phone) is a single contact in the account and a separate member in each audience they belong to, each with its own status, groups and custom field values. Each member exposes the contact it belongs to in its `contact` property: the contact is the person (data shared by all their audiences, see the `Contacts` operations) and the member is their subscription to this audience.
tags.name: Members

tags.description: Groups are labels you assign to the members of one audience by hand or by rule, to target campaigns and automations. Bulk group actions run in the background and return an async task you follow with `get_async_task`.
tags.name: Groups

tags.description: Segments are saved filters that select the members of an audience matching up to five conditions; who is inside updates by itself as data changes. Bulk segment actions run in the background and return an async task you follow with `get_async_task`.
tags.name: Segments

tags.description: Custom fields store extra data on each member of an audience (company, birthday, interests). Their `template_tag` personalizes emails, and their values are set when you create or update a member.
tags.name: Custom fields

tags.description: Condition fields are the member properties you can filter on in segments, in bulk group actions by conditions and in automation conditions. Each one lists the operators it accepts.
tags.name: Condition fields

tags.description: Merge tags are the placeholders you can use in the emails of an audience to insert member data, custom field values and required links such as the unsubscribe link.
tags.name: Merge tags

tags.description: Embedded and popup sign-up forms of an audience: they add the people who fill them to the audience. Forms made in the new Easymailing panel can be read here but not changed.
tags.name: Subscription forms

tags.description: Quick polls and multi-question surveys that you link to email campaigns to collect answers from your subscribers, and their aggregated results.
tags.name: Surveys

tags.description: One-off email campaigns sent to an audience, some of its groups or a segment: regular newsletters, A/B tests, revalidation and survey campaigns. Create and edit them, send test emails, and send or schedule them.
tags.name: Email campaigns

tags.description: Text message (SMS) campaigns sent to contacts with a confirmed SMS subscription in an audience, some of its groups or a segment. Create and edit them, send test messages, and send or schedule them.
tags.name: SMS campaigns

tags.description: Automated workflows that run a series of steps for the contacts of one audience. You create the automation, give it triggers (what starts it for a contact) and steps (what happens to the contact), then activate it. It starts as a draft and sends nothing until it is active.
tags.name: Automations

tags.description: The events and dates that start an automation for a contact: a form completed, a campaign clicked, an order paid, a date reached, a call from your own system. An automation can have several triggers, and every new automation already gets one manual trigger.
tags.name: Automation triggers

tags.description: The actions an automation performs on each contact once a trigger has started it, arranged as a flow: send an email or an SMS, wait, check a condition and branch, change groups, fields or score, call a webhook, start another automation, jump to another step or unsubscribe the contact.
tags.name: Automation steps

tags.description: Email designs you can assign to campaigns and automations: either your own HTML or a design built with the visual editor.
tags.name: Templates

tags.description: Base designs of your own account that you marked as master in the panel, to start new templates from.
tags.name: Master templates

tags.description: Ready-made email designs offered by Easymailing, with the types and industries to browse them, that you copy into your own templates.
tags.name: Themes

tags.description: Brand styles of the account: colors, fonts, button style, logos and social links that give emails and landing pages their visual identity.
tags.name: Brand settings

tags.description: Online stores (WooCommerce, Shopify, your own shop) connected to an audience, so their customers, products and orders can be tracked and used in automations.
tags.name: Stores

tags.description: Groupings of the products of a store (for example "Shoes"), used to organize the catalog.
tags.name: Product categories

tags.description: The products of a store catalog. Orders refer to them through their variants.
tags.name: Products

tags.description: The purchasable options of a product (size, color), each with its own price and stock. Orders list variants.
tags.name: Product variants

tags.description: The buyers of a store. Each customer is tied to a member of the store's audience, so purchases can be used in segments and automations.
tags.name: Store customers

tags.description: Orders and carts of a store, with the steps of their life (cart, processed, paid, shipped, cancelled, refunded). Each step feeds revenue statistics and can start automations.
tags.name: Orders

tags.description: Email addresses that can appear as the sender (From) of campaigns. Each one must be confirmed by following a link sent to that address.
tags.name: Email senders

tags.description: Names that appear as the sender of SMS messages. Each one is validated before it can be used in SMS campaigns.
tags.name: SMS senders

tags.description: Your own domains authenticated for sending (SPF/DKIM/DMARC records), so campaigns go out with your domain and better deliverability.
tags.name: Sending domains

tags.description: Notifications Easymailing sends to your own server when something happens in an audience (a member subscribes, opens an email, joins a group...), with the log of what was sent.
tags.name: Webhooks

tags.description: Data protection (GDPR) settings shared by the audiences: who is responsible for the data (data managers) and why it is collected (treatment purposes).
tags.name: Privacy

tags.description: The plan of the account and how much of it is used: subscribers, credits, limits, AI cost and SMS credits.
tags.name: Plan & usage

tags.description: Invoices Easymailing has issued to the account for its subscription.
tags.name: Invoices

tags.description: Requests for help sent to the Easymailing support team, and their replies, for the user making the call.
tags.name: Support tickets

tags.description: Many API calls sent at once and run in the background. Each call in the batch is checked against the permissions of the credential that created the batch. A batch belongs to the user who created it: only that user and an account administrator can read, delete or download it; for anyone else it does not exist (404). Batches created before this rule was introduced have no creator and stay visible to every credential of the account until they expire, 15 days after creation.
tags.name: Batch operations

tags.description: Where to follow long operations that run in the background. The operations that return a task are in Groups and Segments; here you check how they went and download their file.
tags.name: Async tasks
